headline: High: xonsh can write and execute shell commands while the paired awesome-list has no runtime safeguards, creating default-capability conflict and downstream misuse risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. agent_a is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, while agent_b has stdin/stdout and filesystem access but no shared channel, clipboard, or MCP path to ingest agent_a outputs by default.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies agent_a text into agent_b stdin as instructions, injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected; do not pipe outputs between them.
If copying text manually, strip instruction-like content first.
Use a read-only review step before any downstream execution.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has no egress, while agent_b can read/write filesystem contents and broad network egress. There is no shared workspace or secret-handling evidence, so leakage is not default, but any shared files could be exposed by agent_b.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, agent_b can read files that agent_a references.
IF sensitive files are present in agent_b's workspace, broad egress can transmit them.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace.
Disable network access for agent_b during review runs.
Mount only the minimum files needed for agent_b.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no runtime capabilities, but agent_b can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, read and write the filesystem, and use stdin/stdout. If both are aimed at the same mutable workspace, agent_b can overwrite artifacts without coordination; uncertainty is limited because agent_a is non-runnable.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to operate on the same writable directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF agent_b is run concurrently with another writer, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time.
Use file locks or a single-writer wrapper.
Snapshot the workspace before agent_b runs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a curated list, so its output can be treated as authoritative references, while agent_b can execute shell commands and act on stdin/stdout. If agent_b consumes agent_a-derived recommendations without verification, mistakes can cascade into incorrect commands or edits; no built-in verification is documented.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a's recommendations as execution guidance without a human review step, errors can propagate.
IF agent_a content is copied into agent_b prompts, agent_b may act on unverified instructions.
mitigations: Ask agent_b to restate assumptions before acting.
Use a checklist to verify commands against source docs.
Limit agent_b to dry-run mode where possible.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced. agent_a touches no data classes and agent_b's documented data classes are generic engineering artifacts, so there is no compliance pathway to assess from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into agent_b's workspace, a separate compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Add a retention policy review if sensitive data is later introduced.
